function: system: over-the-air FL aggregation design (area 7: learner/jammer scheduling, power scaling, post-processing factor) with single-antenna devices and BS, scalar channel gains, no RIS (p. 4).
notes: Exclude, reason system. Research article (not survey). Over-the-air FL: the learned element is the CNN trained across the devices on MNIST (p. 11), so no_learning does not apply; the scheduling of learners and jammers, the power scaling factor and the post-processing factor are optimized with classical algorithms (closed forms, SU, SP-SJR, AO; p. 7-11) as the design of the analog over-the-air aggregation, which is the problem of area 7, so above_phy and function do not apply. Every link is single antenna and there is no RIS: p. 4: "Assume that h_{n,B} in R+ and h_{n,E} in R+ are the channel gain coefficients linking device n with the BS and the eavesdropper"; eqs. (5)-(6) on p. 4 superpose scalar-gain signals and Fig. 1 (p. 4) shows one scalar fading gain per device; the simulation setting (p. 11) gives only the noise variances and a 30 dBm power limit. No antenna array, beamformer or RIS appears anywhere in the text; MIMO appears only in titles of cited references. Quantitative results exist (p. 11-12), so results would not apply.
